text:
alex: Quick heads-up — hit a crash in the Python SDK when connecting to Dedicated behind our HTTP proxy + a custom CA. Looks like the client recreates the session during a retry and the TLS handshake fails against the proxy's cert.

marta: ugh. can you paste a minimal repro? which client (sync/async)?

alex: sync + async both affected. repro snippet: 
```python
from redwood import Client
cli = Client(base_url='https://dedicated.us.redwood', api_key='REDACTED', proxy='http://10.1.2.3:3128', ca_bundle='/etc/redwood/custom-ca.pem')
resp = cli.chat.create(model='rw-v1', input='hello')
```

error: 
```
aiohttp.client_exceptions.ClientConnectorCertificateError: Certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate
 (ssl: True)
```
Seems only happens when a request is retried by our retry middleware; first attempt works, retry path reuses a new session without the custom ca.

samir: do we set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE / SSL_CERT_FILE env in the Dedicated container? that usually helps for requests + urllib3.

alex: I tried REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and SSL_CERT_FILE — sync requests path picks it up, but aiohttp (async) path ignores it. Also it's brittle — env var isn't user-friendly for Private customers who want explicit config via the SDK.

jessica: is this the pool/adapter re-creating the connector? urllib3's PoolManager and aiohttp's TCPConnector behave differently on reconnect. We might be overwriting ssl_context on retry.

alex: exactly. dug into client.py — in RetryPolicy we close and recreate sessions on certain errors; when we recreate for async client we call `aiohttp.ClientSession()` without passing ssl=ssl_context. Sync client path uses `requests.Session()` but we forgot to inject certs into the session's mount in some code paths.

marta: thanks for the diagnosis. proposals: 1) add explicit `ca_bundle` / `ssl_context` kwarg to Client that is passed through to both sync and async internals 2) make retries reuse the same session or reapply ssl params on recreation 3) doc the env-var workarounds. which is preferred?

alex: i vote for (1) + (2). (1) is API forward-compatible and clearer for Dedicated/Private. (2) protects against future bugs. I'll draft a patch for both clients.

samir: small note: for sync requests, we should ensure `Session.verify` points to the file path or an SSLContext with loaded CA bundle. For async, create an `ssl.SSLContext()` and load_verify_locations(cafile=...) then pass to `TCPConnector(ssl=ctx)` and ensure session uses that connector.

jessica: add a regression test that spins up a tiny proxy that terminates TLS with the custom CA, then assert client works across a forced retry (simulate 502 then 200). keep it flaky-free by controlling backoff.

infra-bot: FYI Dedicated proxy teams: we saw similar reports in telemetry last week — it was tagged as 'proxy-tls-terminated' but we didn't have repros. tagging infra for follow-up.

alex: workaround for now I left in the sample app: set `ca_bundle` arg to Client and keep session pinned by passing `max_retries=0` (not great). will open PR with tests.

marta: please file an issue and assign to me. include a short note on user impact and examples for Private customers who mount certs at /etc/redwood/custom-ca.pem.

alex: opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/489 (WIP) — adds `Client(..., ca_bundle='/path')` and preserves ssl on retry for async + sync. PTAL @marta @samir

samir: looks good at a glance. a couple nits on naming (ssl_context vs ca_bundle) — prefer `ca_bundle` string path for ergonomics and `ssl_context` for advanced use. add both?

jessica: agree. expose `ca_bundle` (str) and `ssl_context` (SSLContext) on the constructor, validate they are not both set to conflicting values.

alex: noted. i'll update the PR, add tests, and add a small blurb to the devex docs for Dedicated/Private on how to configure proxy + CA.

marta: thanks — assign to platform/py-sdk for release in next patch. once merged we'll add a short migration note. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks all. will follow up with the PR changes and CI results.
